chapter: Local 94, Local 808 and the union convention
title: Tony Twist's lawsuit against Zigfields and the Local 94 by-law
summary: After Local 94 had to fight Zigfields in court, Fields wins a by-law for civil suits at the local's expense.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

So finally a new club, two or three years ago, opened up in Tulsa, Zigfields, and a boy got a gig in there, a nice paying gig, right locally, which you know yourself, about twenty five hundred a week right there on location, and they had some kind of trouble with the crowd and he fired him without notice, and the boy filed charges, and he got on the burner, he was just very intense about the way it was done and everything and they still refused to pay him, they weren't going to pay him. The put the club on default and the club turned around then and filed charges against him and this thing had to be fought out in court and put a strain on ninety four.
The union there, on ninety four and Tony Twist, the leader.
So then, to protect their own skin, the union had to fight. Well, we won it, but it cost money and so I brought it up after that that
in our by-laws that anytime a contract was deposited and everything was as it should be and they they couldn't get it, (inaudible) that they go to civil court and at the local's expense.

The secretary kind of didn't know and this and that, but finally they put it on three reasons, and it went overwhelmingly that in other words--and I explained to them--I said we had this past example that--we didn't know whether Tony Twist was going to win that--and of course the secretary said, before it was passed, what are you trying to do, break the union? He said, do you know how much that lawsuit cost? I said that's a point to have something to show in there that we do for the musicians.
That was the orchestra leader that filed the lawsuit against Zigfields.

Yes, he filed charges against Zigfields and of course, he was right and they put Zigfields on default, but then Zigfields turned around and put the union on restrainer, that they couldn't do this. So we went to court.
Did he get his money, did Tony Twist get his money?
Yeah. The filed for the two weeks work, you know, (inaudible). But the whole point was that when I got over there and that vote came up, it went over overwhelmingly.
